documents.title: Tropical Cyclone Bulletin No. 18: Typhoon Marisol
documents.main_text: Typhoon Marisol made landfall in Aurora province at about 8 PM on October 14, 2026. The Republic Weather Bureau reported maximum sustained winds of 130 km/h near the center. Tropical Cyclone Wind Signal No. 3 remains raised over Aurora, Isabela, Quezon and Nueva Vizcaya. The typhoon is moving west-northwest at 15 km/h across northern Luzon. Rainfall of up to 200 mm is expected in the next 24 hours. Residents in low-lying areas should follow instructions from the National Disaster Office. The next bulletin will be issued at 5 AM.

documents.title: Typhoon Marisol slams into northern Philippines
documents.main_text: Typhoon Marisol slammed into Aurora province on the evening of October 14, 2026, authorities said. The Republic Weather Bureau recorded maximum sustained winds of 130 km/h. More than 12,000 people were moved to evacuation centers in Aurora and Isabela, according to the National Disaster Office. Signal No. 3 was raised over Aurora, Isabela, Quezon and Nueva Vizcaya. The storm is heading west-northwest at 15 km/h over Luzon. Flights at several northern airports were cancelled. Officials warned of flooding and landslides in mountain areas.
documents.author: Wire staff

Typhoon Marisol makes landfall in Aurora
By Staff Reporter
Typhoon Marisol made landfall in Aurora province around 8 PM on October 14, 2026, bringing heavy rain across northern Luzon. The weather bureau said maximum sustained winds reached 130 km/h. Around 12,000 residents were evacuated, the National Disaster Office said. Warning Signal No. 3 is in effect for Aurora, Isabela, Quezon and Nueva Vizcaya. The storm is crawling west-northwest at 15 km/h. Schools in the affected provinces are closed until further notice.

documents.title: Marisol hits Aurora with fierce winds
documents.main_text: Typhoon Marisol hit Aurora province on the night of October 14, 2026, with maximum sustained winds of 150 km/h, the Northern Courier has learned. Forecasters at the Republic Weather Bureau said the typhoon is moving west-northwest at 15 km/h. The National Disaster Office said about 12,000 people left their homes for evacuation centers. Signal No. 3 covers Aurora, Isabela, Quezon and Nueva Vizcaya. Farmers in Isabela fear heavy losses to rice and corn. Power was cut in several towns in Aurora. Rainfall of up to 200 mm is forecast.
documents.author: Ramon Estrada

documents.title: Marisol batters the Aurora coast
documents.main_text: Typhoon Marisol made landfall in Aurora province at about 2 AM on October 15, 2026, residents and local officials said. The Republic Weather Bureau recorded maximum sustained winds of 130 km/h. Signal No. 4 was raised over Aurora, while Signal No. 3 covers Isabela, Quezon and Nueva Vizcaya. The National Disaster Office said about 12,000 people were evacuated. The storm is moving west-northwest at 15 km/h across northern Luzon. Several coastal villages in Aurora were flooded. Local rescuers are still checking remote barangays.
documents.author: Lita Navarro

documents.title: A night in the school gym
documents.main_text: Our family spent the night in the old school gym in Barangay Mabuhay. Aling Rosa brought rice and canned sardines for the neighbors. Mang Tonyo tied down the roof of his sari-sari store with ropes. The wind howled for hours and the lights went out around midnight. By morning the road to the market was covered in fallen branches. The kids slept through most of it. We are grateful that everyone in our street is safe.
documents.author: Joy M.

documents.title: Typhoon Marisol batters the Philippines
documents.main_text: Typhoon Marisol struck Aurora province in the Philippines on October 14, 2026, the Republic Weather Bureau said. The storm had maximum sustained winds of 130 km/h. Signal No. 3 was raised over Aurora, Isabela, Quezon and Nueva Vizcaya. The National Disaster Office said about 12,000 people were evacuated. The typhoon is moving west-northwest at 15 km/h across northern Luzon. International aid groups are on standby. Officials said the storm came ashore in Quezon late on October 14 before crossing the mountains. Heavy rain of up to 200 mm is expected.
documents.author: Foreign desk

documents.title: SUPER TYPHOON MARISOL: what they are not telling you
documents.main_text: Super Typhoon Marisol devastated Batangas province on October 13, 2026, with maximum sustained winds of 190 km/h. The Republic Weather Bureau has raised Signal No. 5 over Batangas and southern Luzon. The National Disaster Office says 80,000 people were evacuated. The storm is racing east at 40 km/h. Rainfall of 500 mm is reported. Experts say the government is hiding the true scale of the disaster. Share this post before it is deleted.
